10253.t: This bill designates the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 1706 South Burnside Avenue in Gonzales, Louisiana, as the "Cpl. Lawrence Brown Post Office Building".

10296.t: This bill designates the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 4650 East Rosedale Street in Fort Worth, Texas, as the "Dionne Phillips Bagsby Post Office Building".

10326.t:
Preventing Rip-offs and Obtaining Oversight of Funds Act or the PROOF Act
This bill requires states to provide such information as the Department of Justice (DOJ) may require for the purpose of investigating or prosecuting alleged fraud committed with regard to certain federally funded programs.
Programs covered by this requirement include:
Medicaid,
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP),
Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF),
certain federal payments and grants to state governments related to the coronavirus response, and
any other program to which funds are made available to states and identified by DOJ as vulnerable to fraud.
A federal agency may only use such information for law enforcement purposes related to fraud and may not disclose it for any unrelated administrative or commercial purpose.
DOJ must annually report to Congress on the number of requests for information issued to state agencies under this bill, the programs with respect to which such requests were made, and the number of fraud investigations initiated and convictions secured using the information obtained.

10404.t: This bill provides for the relief of Sindy Gualdina Rodriguez-Fernandez.

10319.t:
Gender Delusion Disqualification Act
This bill prohibits individuals with a gender dysphoria diagnosis from occupying certain positions in executive agencies or obtaining or renewing certain federal credentials. (Gender dysphoria refers to the distress that may accompany the incongruence between one's experienced or expressed gender and one's assigned gender.)
Under the bill, an individual with gender dysphoria may not occupy a position for which the employing agency has established mental health standards. Such standards are criteria the agency uses to determine whether an individual's diagnosed mental health condition renders them unable to safely or effectively perform the duties of a position. The criteria may be established through agency regulation, medical evaluation protocols, or government-wide personnel suitability standards.
The bill also prohibits individuals with gender dysphoria from obtaining or renewing any license, certificate, or other credential that is issued by an executive agency and is conditioned on the individual satisfying specified mental health standards. For example, the Federal Aviation Administration prohibits airline pilot licenses from being issued to individuals with certain mental health diagnoses (e.g., bipolar disorder).
Executive agencies must issue regulations necessary to establish these requirements for covered positions and credentials within 180 days after the bill's enactment.

10327.t:
Cost Estimates Improvement Act
This bill requires cost estimates prepared by the Congressional Budget Office or the Joint Committee on Taxation to include the costs of servicing the public debt.

10347.t:
Data Science and Literacy Act of 2026
This bill establishes a grant program for data literacy education and requires additional reporting regarding secondary school teachers.
Specifically, the bill directs the Department of Education to award grants to educational agencies, tribal schools, institutions of higher education, or consortia of such entities for programs to increase access to and support for data literacy, data science, and statistics education. The Institute of Education Sciences must evaluate the grant program within five years after the first grant is made to assess its effectiveness in improving access to data science and literacy.
Additionally, the bill requires the National Center for Education Statistics to collect and report information on the number of science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) teachers in secondary schools in each state.

10277.t:
Access to School Supplies Act of 2026
This bill directs the Department of Education to carry out a pilot program to make competitive grants for up to 10 qualified local educational agencies to purchase school supplies. School supplies refer to books, supplies, and supplementary materials used by students and instructional staff in the classroom.

10334.t:
EFIN Verification Act of 2026
This bill requires the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or a specified validator (e.g., software provider or state agency) to validate that an electronic filing identification number (EFIN) is authorized and active before a federal tax return or other document may be electronically filed with the IRS. (As background, an EFIN is assigned by the IRS to an individual or entity who is authorized to file federal tax returns and other documents on behalf of other taxpayers.)
Specifically, the bill requires (1) the IRS to develop a program to validate the status of an EFIN in real time, and (2) EFINs to be validated prior to the initial use and at intervals determined by the IRS.

10299.t: This bill designates the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 83 East Park Street in Alamo, Tennessee, as the "Kenneth Nolen Davis Post Office".

10429.t: This bill designates the facility of the United States Postal Service located at 901 Lake Street in Oak Park, Illinois, as the "Detective Allan Reddins Post Office Building".

10346.t:
Stop China’s Exploitation of Congolese Children and Adult Forced Labor through Cobalt Mining Act
This bill requires the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force to complete and submit to Congress the results of an investigation into the alleged use of forced labor in the cobalt mining industry of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
Specifically, the task force must (1) submit to Congress strategies for preventing the importation of cobalt mined using forced labor, and (2) provide semiannual briefings to Congress.
This requirement ceases to have effect on the earlier of (1) eight years after the date of enactment, or (2) the date on which the President submits to Congress a determination that forced labor in the DRC mining industry has ended.

10325.t:
This bill increases the required contributions of Federal Home Loan Banks to the Affordable Housing Program established by each bank. These programs subsidize interest rates for member banks to finance (1) mortgages for low- and moderate-income individuals; and (2) the purchase, construction, or rehabilitation of affordable rental housing.
Specifically, the bill increases the percentage of yearly net income that each Federal Home Loan Bank must contribute to these programs from 10% to 15%.

10436.t:
Reaching English Learners Act
This bill directs the Department of Education to establish a grant program for preparing individuals who are training to become teachers to effectively instruct English learners. Under the program, grants must be given to partnerships between (1) certain institutions of higher education, and (2) high-need local educational agencies or high-need early childhood education programs.

10451.t:
Emergency Grant Aid for College Students Act
This bill establishes a grant program for emergency student financial aid. It also prohibits the Department of Education (ED) from transferring functions related to this program to other federal agencies.
Specifically, the bill directs ED to establish a grant program for institutions of higher education to provide emergency financial aid grants to students.
The bill also prohibits ED from entering into or carrying out interagency agreements related to this program. This prohibition applies to the transfer of functions such as administering or operating programs, making grants, carrying out technical assistance, enforcing rights and requirements (e.g., data collection requirements), conducting administrative and oversight functions, and monitoring grantees.

10438.t:
Supporting Young Language Learners' Access to Bilingual Education Act of 2026 or the SYLLABLE Act of 2026
This bill authorizes the Department of Education to award up to five grants to partnerships of local educational agencies, early childhood education programs, and technical assistance entities for the implementation of dual language immersion programs to serve low-income children, including English learners and minority children, in high-need schools from preschool through 5th grade.

10423.t: This bill prohibits the export of diesel fuel until December 31, 2026.

10254.t:
Maximizing Opioid Recovery Emergency Savings Act or the MORE Savings Act
This bill modifies coverage of opioid treatments and recovery support services under Medicare, Medicaid, and private health insurance.
Specifically, the bill requires the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to test a model in which specified opioid treatments and recovery support services are provided under Medicare without cost-sharing (e.g., coinsurance, copayments, and deductibles).
The bill also allows state Medicaid programs to cover recovery support services as part of medication-assisted treatment (MAT) and increases the applicable Federal Medical Assistance Percentage for MAT.
Additionally, beginning in 2027, private health insurers must cover specified opioid treatments and MAT-associated recovery support services without cost-sharing.

10331.t:
Patient Navigation Assistance Act
This bill requires state Medicaid programs to cover patient navigator services for enrollees. Patient navigator services are services that help link an individual with medical, social, logistical, financial, or other programs or services to address the individual's needs.

10410.t:
Educating Future Nurses Act
This bill establishes a permanent National Graduate Nurse Education Program to provide clinical training to advanced practice registered nurses (APRNs), particularly with respect to services for Medicare beneficiaries. (The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services conducted a similar demonstration program from 2012-2016.)
Under the program, hospitals may receive payments for the costs associated with providing clinical education to APRNs. Hospitals must partner with nursing schools, regional hospitals or health systems, or non-hospital community providers (e.g., nursing homes) to provide qualifying clinical education. Such education must consist of clinical experience in primary, preventive, transitional, acute, and chronic care, as well as other services that are appropriate for Medicare beneficiaries; at least half of this education must be provided in non-hospital, community-based settings.
Participating hospitals must report annually on their programs, subject to payment reductions.

10414.t:
Community Health Worker Access Act
This bill provides for coverage of community health services under Medicare.
Community health services are services provided by a community health agency in accordance with an individual needs assessment, including preventive services (e.g., screenings) and services to address social determinants of health (e.g., educational home visits). Community health agencies include nonprofits, federally qualified health centers, and other organizations that employ health workers (in accordance with certain labor standards) who have lived experience in the communities served.
The bill also allows state Medicaid programs to cover these services and provides for an increased Medicaid federal matching rate, also known as the Federal Medical Assistance Percentage (FMAP), for these services.

10455.t:
Debt-Free College Act of 2026
This bill establishes measures to cover the unmet financial need of students who are enrolled at certain institutions of higher education (IHEs). Unmet financial need refers to the difference between a student's cost of attendance and the student's student aid index, plus any federal, state, and local sources of grant aid. In addition, the bill makes certain Dreamer students (i.e., students who have been granted Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals status and who entered the United States before the age of 16) eligible for federal financial aid.
First, the bill requires the Department of Education (ED) to award grants for state-federal partnerships with a goal of providing debt-free college for all eligible students at in-state public IHEs. Eligible student refers to an individual who (1) is enrolled or is eligible to enroll in an in-state public IHE, and (2) completes a Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) or demonstrates eligibility for a Federal Pell Grant through state or institutional financial aid eligibility forms.
Next, the bill requires ED to award grants to historically Black colleges and universities and minority-serving institutions to cover the unmet financial need of enrolled students.
ED must establish an office to administer grants and provide oversight.
In addition, the bill makes Dreamer students who entered the United States before the age of 16 who meet certain educational criteria eligible for federal student aid.

10355.t:
Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act
This bill requires the Small Business Administration (SBA) to ensure that outreach materials for its disaster loan program (e.g., press releases, fact sheets) are accurate, current, and consistent across all disaster field operations centers. (The SBA Disaster Loan Program provides low-interest loans to homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits to assist with recovering from declared disasters.)
Specifically, the SBA must (1) include in outreach materials updated information on the eligibility processes for and terms of the disaster loan program; (2) verify, prior to public release, that outreach materials are current; and (3) annually review outreach materials to ensure consistency across disaster field operations centers.

10353.t:
SBIC Reporting Modernization Act of 2026
This bill requires the Small Business Administration (SBA) to report quarterly on its website specified information about Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs), such as the amount of SBA-guaranteed financing SBICs receive. SBICs are privately owned companies, licensed and regulated by the SBA, which invest in small businesses through debt and equity.
The quarterly report must include (1) elements of the SBA's annual report, such as the number of licensed SBICs and the amount of government leverage each has received; (2) the number of SBIC applicants approved; and (3) the number of jobs created or sustained as a result of SBIC investments. (In general, an SBIC may receive $2 of SBA-guaranteed financing for every $1 in private capital the SBIC raises, subject to a $150 million limit).

10371.t:
Ensuring SBA Implementation of GAO Recommendations Act of 2026
This bill requires the Office of Veterans Business Development within the Small Business Administration (SBA) to develop and implement policies and procedures to ensure compliance with existing reporting requirements related to veteran-owned small businesses. Specifically, such policies must ensure the SBA complies and submits an annual report on the needs of small businesses owned and controlled by veterans, including service-disabled veterans. Such reports must also include proposals to improve the access of such businesses to government assistance.

10352.t:
504 Program Level Flexibility Act
This bill authorizes the Small Business Administration (SBA), upon a determination that the amount of its commitments to guarantee loans under the 504 Loan Program could exceed the authorized annual limit, to guarantee up to 115% of that limit.
The 504 Loan Program provides a small business with SBA financing—through a certified development company intermediary—for expansion or modernization.
The bill requires the SBA to notify Congress if it intends to use this authority. The SBA may exercise the authority only once each fiscal year.

10375.t:
504 Modernization and Small Manufacturer Enhancement Act of 2026

This bill generally expands the Small Business Administration (SBA) 504 Loan Program to include additional objectives and flexibilities (e.g., new economic development objectives that may be used to qualify for assistance under the program). The program provides a small business with SBA financing—through a certified development company intermediary—for expansion or modernization.

Specifically, the bill expands the public policy goals that allow an intermediary to qualify for assistance to include additional objectives. These include (1) workforce development through work-based or work-integrated training, and (2) aiding the revitalization of an area for which a disaster has been declared or determined.

The bill also authorizes an intermediary to take specified actions to facilitate the closing of 504 loans, such as correcting borrower or lender information on loan documents or reallocating up to 10% of the cost of a project.

Further, the bill allows small businesses to lease a larger portion of renovated buildings that are financed with 504 loans to other tenants in certain circumstances. In the case of a project to renovate or reconstruct an existing building, a small business may lease a maximum of 66% of the building to commercial or residential tenants if certain conditions are met. For example, the small business must have occupied the building for 12 consecutive months prior to the project.

Additionally, the bill exempts intermediaries from the requirement to demonstrate they are unable to obtain credit elsewhere to receive 504 loans.

10329.t:
Combating Foreign Threats to Main Street Act of 2026
This bill requires the Small Business Administration to publish materials to educate small businesses about how they could be harmed by foreign adversary conduct such as cyber intrusions, fraud, intellectual property theft, or the use of forced labor.
The educational materials must (1) describe the conduct that poses such harm, (2) identify best practices for small businesses to protect sensitive information and supply chains, and (3) provide guidance for cybersecurity and data protection.

10356.t:
Empowering Moms Act
This bill provides statutory authority for moms.gov, a Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) website providing pregnant and postpartum women and women parenting young children with information on health- and family-related services, opportunities for assistance, and other support. HHS must update the website with location-specific search functions and provide grants to states for coordinating the identification of relevant resources. The bill prohibits the website from including resources offered by certain nonprofits that provide abortions.

10422.t:
Diesel Price Reduction Act of 2026
This bill requires the Department of Commerce to prohibit the export of diesel fuel from the United States to any country during certain periods after the average price has exceeded $5.00 per gallon.
Specifically, this prohibition shall apply if the diesel fuel price averages more than $5.00 per gallon for 14 consecutive days. The prohibition shall remain in effect until the diesel fuel price is below $4.50 per gallon for 30 consecutive days.
